rule: Threshold pace estimated from a 30-min pace-locked conversational treadmill run = average pace / 1.25 (i.e. that pace is assumed to be 80% of threshold speed); low confidence until a 30-min TT.
summary: The ratio is consistent with physiology: in competitive athletes VT1 and RCT fell at 67% and 84% of max speed (VT1 ~80% of RCT speed), and a 120k-runner analysis placed the Z1/Z2 boundary at 82.3% of critical speed. The 'last comfortable talk' pace tracks VT1 on average, but speech-difficulty ratings vary widely between people, and a runner may lock a pace well below VT1, so the estimate is likely conservative (too slow) with an individual error around +/-10%. The low-confidence label and 'confirm with a 30-min TT' rule are the right handling; no study tests the 1.25 divisor itself.

sources.note: VT at 67 +/- 9% and RCT at 84 +/- 6% of Vmax (ratio ~0.80), wide individual spread
